scoring_justification: The checker recomputes the monotonic trend and directly verifies PRDF first-peak distances against published reference values, achieving T1 recompute for both artifacts.

hidden_assets.purpose: PRDF first-peak reference distances for Si-O, O-O, Si-Si pairs.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Vashishta et al., Phys. Rev. B 41, 12197 (1990) and Mozzi & Warren, J. Appl. Crystallogr. 2, 164 (1969), as cited in the paper.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Distances taken directly from the paper's description: Si-O ~1.61 Å, O-O ~2.6 Å, Si-Si ~3.1 Å.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are established interatomic distances for amorphous silica, independently verified by prior simulation and X-ray diffraction experiments and explicitly referenced in the paper.

outputs.description: First-peak positions of the partial radial distribution functions for Si-O, O-O, and Si-Si pairs. These are compared to known interatomic distances from prior simulation and experiment.

Tensile strength (maximum stress) for each cooling rate. The relation that higher cooling rate leads to lower tensile strength is verified by checking monotonic decreasing order in the submitted rows.

output_contract.notes: The agent must generate amorphous samples at multiple cooling rates and perform full tensile loading simulations, not merely report a guessed trend. The structural audit on tensile strength checks monotonic decrease; the reference match on PRDF checks proximity to established distances (within a hidden tolerance). At least two cooling rates must appear in the tensile strength output.

steps.description: Verify PRDF first-peak distances match Si-O≈1.61 Å, O-O≈2.60 Å, Si-Si≈3.10 Å within ±0.1 Å.
Check that tensile strength decreases monotonically with increasing cooling rate (at least two distinct rates must be present).
